title: Equality-free classical first-order sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)

summary: Build equality-free quantified sequent certificates with explicit eigenparameters, expand identities and prove soundness, including languages without ground terms.
abstract: A proof about every object must treat its chosen object as arbitrary, while a proof that some object exists may use a particular term. We make that difference visible in a classical sequent calculus, where each finite set of formulas offers alternative conclusions. Moving negations to relation atoms gives a signed syntax connected exactly to the existing first-order formulas. Seven rules then generate finite proof certificates, including a quantified rule that introduces a fresh parameter without constraining the surrounding formulas. We prove soundness, construct identities for compound quantified formulas, and explain why temporary witness names are needed even for a closed assertion in a language without constants.
